# Wirecard and Jan Marsalek: Evidence-Bounded Reconstruction of the Public-Fraud Trail

## Executive summary

As of **1 October 2026**, the benchmark returned only two usable sources: a 28 April 2020 Wirecard disclosure concerning a KPMG special investigation, and a November 2020 European Parliament-commissioned policy study on the supervisory implications of the Wirecard case: [SRC-001 — Wirecard AG: KPMG delivers report on special investigation](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation) and [SRC-002 — What are the wider supervisory implications of the Wirecard case?](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf).

Those sources support a limited but clear reconstruction:

1. Wirecard publicly represented in April 2020 that KPMG had not identified incriminating evidence of balance-sheet forgery and had found no significant matters requiring adjustment of the 2016–2018 accounts. That is evidence of **what Wirecard stated**, not independent verification of the statement. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
2. The same disclosure acknowledged limitations in the available data, documentation and organization, stated that some relevant data were controlled by third parties, and disclosed that the annual accounts and annual press conference would be delayed. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
3. The policy study later assessed that all five lines of defense against corporate fraud and deception failed in one way or another: Wirecard’s internal controls, supervisory board, external audit, financial-reporting and auditing oversight bodies, and BaFin. This is an **authorial assessment**, not an adjudicated finding supplied by the returned evidence. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)
4. The returned evidence does **not** support factual claims about the alleged missing cash, the €1.9 billion or €2 billion trust-account issue, June 2020 disclosures, insolvency, detailed EY findings, or Jan Marsalek’s disappearance and reported whereabouts. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation) [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

Accordingly, the evidence permits a documented chronology of Wirecard’s April 2020 public position, audit uncertainty and the later policy assessment of supervisory failure, but it does not permit a source-supported chronology connecting those events to Marsalek’s disappearance or to the later missing-cash allegations.

## Evidence base and evidentiary rules

### Returned sources

The evidence set contains two unique source IDs.

- **SRC-001** is a Wirecard AG inside-information disclosure dated **28 April 2020 at 07:52 CET/CEST** concerning the KPMG special investigation. The announcement identifies DGAP, a service of EQS Group AG, as the transmission service and states that Wirecard AG was solely responsible for the announcement’s content. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **SRC-002** is the study *What are the wider supervisory implications of the Wirecard case?*, identified as an Economic Governance Support Unit study, document PE 651.385, dated November 2020 and requested by the European Parliament’s ECON Committee. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

SRC-002 states that its manuscript was completed in May 2020 and that its opinions are the authors’ responsibility and do not necessarily represent the official position of the European Parliament. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

### Classification of evidence

The sources should not be treated as having the same evidentiary status.

- Statements in SRC-001 about what KPMG supposedly found are **Wirecard’s corporate representations** of the special investigation.
- Statements in SRC-002 about failed lines of defense, institutional architecture and regulatory reform are **the authors’ assessments and recommendations**.
- The absence of a topic from the returned excerpts is not proof that the event did not occur; it means only that the event is **not established by the benchmark evidence available here**.
- Search-query wording is not evidence. The query terms concerning €1.9 billion, trust accounts, insolvency, ESMA, APAS, the Bundestag or Marsalek’s whereabouts cannot be used as factual support because the returned source excerpts do not contain those facts.

## Source-supported chronology

### 28 April 2020: Wirecard announces the KPMG special-audit result

Wirecard stated that it had received the special audit report from KPMG in the early hours of 28 April 2020 and that the report would be published as soon as possible on Wirecard’s transparency webpage. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

Wirecard’s central public statement was: **“Incriminating evidence for the public allegations of balance sheet forgery has not been identified.”** Because the statement appears in Wirecard’s own disclosure, it establishes Wirecard’s public position rather than independently establishing the truth of the underlying proposition. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

Wirecard further stated that, across the four areas examined—Third Party Acquiring, Merchant Cash Advance/Digital Lending, and business activities in India and Singapore—KPMG had made no significant findings requiring adjustment of the 2016–2018 annual accounts. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

### Data limitations disclosed by Wirecard

The disclosure also contained qualifications that are important to the audit-uncertainty trail.

Wirecard stated that, under KPMG’s increased forensic requirements, not all data needed to prove revenues for the relevant years could be obtained because the required data were primarily controlled by third parties. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

Wirecard stated that it had provided KPMG with more than 200 million data sets relating to December 2019 and that the resulting forensic audit had revealed no deviations between reported revenues and account balances. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

Wirecard also stated that KPMG had identified documentation and organizational weaknesses. Wirecard said those weaknesses had already been identified internally and were being addressed through a Global Compliance Organization and the support of external consultants. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

These statements create an evidence-supported distinction between:

- Wirecard’s public assertion that no incriminating evidence had been identified;
- Wirecard’s acknowledgment that not all requested data were available;
- Wirecard’s assertion that the data it supplied for December 2019 showed no deviations; and
- Wirecard’s acknowledgment of documentation and organizational weaknesses.

The returned evidence does not independently resolve how those qualifications affected the reliability or completeness of the special investigation.

### 28 April 2020: Delay to annual accounts and audit completion

Wirecard stated that publication of its annual accounts and the annual press conference would not take place on 30 April 2020. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

Wirecard also stated that it would coordinate with E&Y concerning when audit measures could be completed, taking account of COVID-19 restrictions and the completion of the KPMG report. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

The returned sources do not establish whether EY had refused to sign the accounts, identified specific irregularities, issued a qualification, resigned, or reached any conclusion about cash, trust accounts or financial-statement misstatement. Those possibilities must therefore remain unresolved.

### Later assessment of the oversight structure

SRC-002 states that the Wirecard case was surprising because signals suggesting fraudulent behavior had existed years before its eventual revelation. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The study assesses that all five lines of defense against corporate fraud and deception failed in one way or another:

1. Wirecard’s internal control system;
2. Wirecard’s supervisory board;
3. external audit;
4. oversight bodies for financial reporting and auditing; and
5. BaFin as market supervisor. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The study identifies what it calls a flawed market and institutional oversight architecture as the root cause in its analysis. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

This assessment supplies an institutional interpretation of the case, but the returned excerpt does not provide a detailed event-by-event account attributing a specific omission, decision or legal violation to a named person or institution.

## Public statements and audit uncertainty

### Wirecard’s public position

The April disclosure presented a favorable account of the KPMG special investigation. Wirecard said that no incriminating evidence of balance-sheet forgery had been identified and that no significant findings required adjustment of the 2016–2018 accounts in the specified business areas. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

At the same time, the disclosure did not describe an entirely unrestricted evidentiary process. Wirecard said that KPMG’s forensic requirements were higher and that not all required data could be obtained because third parties controlled the relevant information. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

The resulting evidence picture is therefore not simply “KPMG cleared Wirecard.” The returned evidence supports the narrower formulation that **Wirecard said KPMG had not identified incriminating evidence and had not found significant matters requiring adjustment, while Wirecard also disclosed data limitations and weaknesses in documentation and organization**. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

### KPMG

The source identifies KPMG as the auditing company that supplied the special audit report to Wirecard. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

The returned excerpt does not reproduce the KPMG report itself. Consequently, KPMG-related conclusions should be expressed as Wirecard’s account of KPMG’s work rather than as independently verified findings.

### EY / E&Y

Wirecard referred to E&Y as the auditor with which it would coordinate concerning completion of audit measures. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

No returned source supplies an EY audit opinion, a refusal to sign, a resignation, a qualification, a finding concerning trust-account balances, or an assessment of the alleged missing cash. No stronger claim about EY is supportable from the evidence returned.

## Alleged missing cash and trust accounts

The returned evidence does not mention allegedly missing cash, €1.9 billion, €2 billion, trustee accounts, trust accounts, bank confirmations, inability to verify cash, June 2020 disclosures, or an insolvency filing. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation) [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

It is therefore not possible, using only the returned benchmark evidence, to establish:

- the amount allegedly missing;
- the date on which any shortage was discovered or disclosed;
- the identity of any bank, trustee or account holder;
- whether cash was absent, misrepresented, inaccessible or merely unverified;
- whether EY, KPMG, Wirecard management, BaFin or another institution knew of the issue;
- whether the alleged cash issue caused the audit delay; or
- whether the alleged cash issue caused or contributed to insolvency.

The appropriate status of this part of the requested trail is **unsupported by the returned evidence**, not disproved.

## Supervisory and regulatory failures

### Five-line assessment

SRC-002’s central institutional assessment is that all five lines of defense failed in one way or another. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The five lines identified by the study are:

- Wirecard’s internal control system;
- its supervisory board;
- external audit;
- oversight bodies for financial reporting and auditing; and
- BaFin as market supervisor. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The study characterizes the underlying problem as a flawed market and institutional oversight architecture and argues that the existing structure was not sufficiently fit to preserve market integrity and investor protection. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

### BaFin

SRC-002 identifies BaFin as the market supervisor and states that BaFin needs stronger supervisory and enforcement powers to fulfill its mandate concerning market integrity and investor protection. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The study recommends broad enforcement powers for BaFin, including forensic and investigative tools. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The returned excerpt does not establish a specific BaFin decision, omission, enforcement action, date, or individual responsibility.

### FREP and financial-reporting enforcement

SRC-002 discusses FREP as a German self-regulatory enforcement body and recommends relegating such bodies to a purely ancillary, optional function. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The returned material does not supply a specific FREP action, finding, date or failure in the Wirecard matter.

### Auditors and internal controls

The study recommends stronger accountability for external auditors so that auditors have greater incentives to detect accounting manipulation and fraud. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

It also recommends requiring listed firms to maintain effective internal-control systems, having the head of internal control report to the supervisory board rather than the management board, and considering internal-control audits. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

These are policy recommendations. They do not, on the returned evidence, establish that a particular auditor, board member or control officer committed a specified violation.

## Jan Marsalek’s disappearance

Neither returned source mentions Jan Marsalek by name. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation) [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The benchmark evidence therefore does not establish:

- when Marsalek disappeared;
- where he was last seen;
- whether he left Germany;
- whether a warrant was issued;
- whether he was reported to be in Russia, Belarus, Moscow or elsewhere;
- whether he used an alias;
- whether an intelligence service was involved;
- whether another person or entity assisted him; or
- whether his disappearance was connected to Wirecard’s financial statements, the alleged missing cash, audit uncertainty or supervisory failures.

No relationship between Marsalek and Wirecard, KPMG, EY, BaFin, FREP, a bank, a trustee or a government or intelligence service should be asserted on the basis of the returned material.

## Relationship network supported by the evidence

### Corporate and audit relationships

- **Wirecard AG → KPMG:** Wirecard stated that KPMG conducted the special investigation and supplied the report received on 28 April 2020. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **Wirecard AG → E&Y:** Wirecard stated that it would coordinate with E&Y concerning completion of audit measures. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **KPMG → audited business areas:** According to Wirecard’s disclosure, the special investigation covered Third Party Acquiring, Merchant Cash Advance/Digital Lending, and business activities in India and Singapore. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **Wirecard AG → Global Compliance Organization:** Wirecard stated that it had established a Global Compliance Organization to address documentation and organizational weaknesses. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **Wirecard AG → external consultants:** Wirecard stated that external consultants supported its remediation efforts. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **Wirecard AG → third parties:** Wirecard stated that third parties controlled much of the data required to prove revenues. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

### Publication and institutional relationships

- **Wirecard AG → DGAP/EQS Group AG:** The announcement was transmitted by DGAP, identified as a service of EQS Group AG. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)
- **ECON Committee → Economic Governance Support Unit:** SRC-002 identifies the study as requested by the European Parliament’s ECON Committee and produced within the Economic Governance Support Unit framework. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)
- **BaFin → market supervision:** SRC-002 identifies BaFin as the market supervisor. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)
- **FREP → financial-reporting enforcement:** SRC-002 discusses FREP as a German self-regulatory financial-reporting enforcement body. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

### Unsupported network links

The returned evidence does not support edges connecting:

- Jan Marsalek to Wirecard;
- Marsalek to a disappearance location;
- Marsalek to Russia, Belarus, Moscow or an intelligence service;
- Marsalek to the alleged missing cash;
- Wirecard to a particular trustee, bank or trust account;
- EY to the alleged €1.9 billion or €2 billion issue;
- BaFin or FREP to a specific trust-account failure; or
- any individual to responsibility for fraud, concealment or supervisory failure.

## Contradictions, tensions and unresolved uncertainty

### Wirecard’s statement versus the policy study

Wirecard stated that incriminating evidence for public allegations of balance-sheet forgery had not been identified and that no significant findings required adjustments to the 2016–2018 accounts. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

SRC-002 later stated that signals suggesting fraudulent behavior had existed years before the eventual revelation and assessed that all five lines of defense failed in one way or another. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

This is a **tension between a contemporaneous corporate representation and a later external policy assessment**. It is not a demonstrated direct contradiction about KPMG’s actual findings because the returned excerpt of SRC-002 does not provide a contrary KPMG conclusion.

### SRC-001 URL and announcement date

The SRC-001 URL contains the path segment `2020/04/22`, while the announcement text is dated 28 April 2020. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

The returned evidence does not explain whether this difference reflects URL creation, publication, migration or another technical matter. The text date is therefore retained as the announcement date, while the URL discrepancy remains unresolved.

### SRC-002 manuscript and publication dates

SRC-002 is identified as a November 2020 study, while its metadata states that the manuscript was completed in May 2020. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The difference may reflect publication after manuscript completion, but the returned evidence does not provide further production details.

### Missing cash and Marsalek

There are no competing accounts in the returned sources concerning the amount, date, responsibility or certainty of the alleged missing-cash issue. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation) [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

There are likewise no competing accounts concerning Marsalek’s disappearance or reported whereabouts because neither returned source mentions him. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation) [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

## Overall conclusion

The returned evidence supports a carefully bounded public-fraud trail beginning with Wirecard’s April 2020 disclosure of the KPMG special-investigation result. Wirecard publicly denied that the investigation had identified incriminating evidence of balance-sheet forgery, reported no significant findings requiring adjustment of the 2016–2018 accounts, acknowledged incomplete access to some data, disclosed organizational and documentation weaknesses, and postponed publication of its annual accounts while coordinating with E&Y on the remaining audit measures. [SRC-001](https://www.wirecard.com/2020/04/22/wirecard-ag-kpmg-special-review-lasts-until-april-27-2020-analysis-so-far-provides-no-evidence-of-balance-sheet-manipulation)

The later policy study supplies an institutional assessment that Wirecard’s internal controls, supervisory board, external audit, financial-reporting and auditing oversight bodies, and BaFin all failed in one way or another. It attributes the broader problem to a flawed market and institutional oversight architecture and recommends stronger supervisory, enforcement, audit-accountability and internal-control arrangements. [SRC-002](https://safe-frankfurt.de/fileadmin/user_upload/editor_common/Policy_Center/SAFE_Policy_White_Paper_74.pdf)

The benchmark evidence does not, however, support the requested later stages of the trail: the alleged missing cash, trust-account amounts, June 2020 disclosures, insolvency, detailed regulatory findings, or Jan Marsalek’s disappearance and whereabouts. Any narrative connecting those matters to Wirecard’s April public statements, the audit process or supervisory failure would exceed the returned evidence.
